hints: Count all multiset permutations, then exclude equal adjacent characters.
For one letter, join selected neighboring copies into blocks.
Combine the numbers of joins for different letters with a polynomial DP.
analogy: Glue some identical neighbors together, then alternate addition and subtraction to remove every arrangement with a forbidden adjacency.
example: For aabc, the six valid orders are abac, abca, acab, acba, baca and caba.
algorithm: For a letter occurring c times, choosing j joins among its c-1 internal gaps leaves c-j blocks and contributes (-1)^j*C(c-1,j)/(c-j)! modulo 1000000007. Convolve these coefficients across all present letters to form dp[t], where t is total joins. The answer is the sum over t of dp[t]*(n-t)!. Precompute factorials, inverse factorials and binomial coefficients modulo the prime.
correctness: Temporarily distinguish identical copies in their fixed relative order. Inclusion-exclusion chooses which gaps between consecutive copies are forced adjacent. A letter with j chosen gaps has c-j indistinguishable blocks; after all choices, arranging n-t blocks gives (n-t)! divided by each block-count factorial. Alternating signs cancel every string with an equal adjacent pair and leave each valid string once.
complexity: For string length n, polynomial convolution over all letters takes O(n^2) time in total and O(n) space with factorial and inverse-factorial tables.
